record.original_question: For a graph G, let tau(G; x) be the polynomial defined by tau(G; x) = sum_{pi in Pi(V)} a(G[pi]) x^{|pi|}. Does tau(G; x) have only real roots for every graph G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with $|V|=n$. Recall that the chromatic polynomial $\chi(G;x)$ counts the proper colorings of $G$, and can be uniquely written in the basis of falling factorials $\langle x\rangle_i := x(x-1)(x-2)\cdots(x-i+1)$ as
$$\chi(G;x)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-i}c_i(G)\,\langle x\rangle_i,$$
where the coefficients $c_i(G)$ are nonnegative integers. Define the $\tau$-polynomial of $G$ by
$$\tau(G;x):=\sum_{i=0}^{n}c_i(G)\,x^{i}.$$

For a subset $B\subseteq V$, let $G[B]$ denote the subgraph of $G$ induced by $B$, and for a set partition $\pi=\{B_1,\ldots,B_k\}\in\Pi(V)$ of $V$, let $G[\pi]$ denote the disjoint union $G[B_1]\sqcup\cdots\sqcup G[B_k]$. For any finite graph $H$, let $a(H)$ denote the number of acyclic orientations of $H$ (so $a(G[\pi])=\prod_{j=1}^{k}a(G[B_j])$). It is known that
$$\tau(G;x)=\sum_{\pi\in\Pi(V)}a(G[\pi])\,x^{|\pi|},$$
where $|\pi|$ is the number of blocks of $\pi$.

Question: Does $\tau(G;x)$ have only real roots for every finite simple graph $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent (2024) survey of open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality. No published resolution has been located; the real-rootedness of the τ-polynomial for all graphs appears to remain open.
